Surah 63: al-Munafiqun (The Hypocrites). It is Madani (revealed in Madinah) by the consensus of scholars, and it has eleven verses. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ (63:1)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah."﴾ Al-Bukhari narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I was with my uncle when I heard Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul say: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.' And he said: 'If we return to al-Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.'"

I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle reported it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions, and they swore that they had not said it. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed them and declared me a liar. I was struck by a grief such as I had never suffered, so I sat in my house. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you ... they are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah" ... the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for me and said: "Indeed Allah has confirmed you." This was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

In al-Tirmidhi, also from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "We went on a military campaign (ghazwah) with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and with us were some Bedouins (a'rab). We would be the first to reach the water, but the Bedouins would get there before us, so a Bedouin would get ahead of his companions, fill the basin, place stones around it, and set a leather mat (nit') over it until his companions arrived." He said: "A man from the Ansar came upon a Bedouin, loosened the rope of his she-camel so it could drink, but the Bedouin refused to let him. So the Ansari pulled out a stone [in al-Tirmidhi: 'he pulled out the plugs of the water'], and the water flowed out. The Bedouin raised a piece of wood and struck the Ansari on the head, wounding him. The Ansari then went to Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, and informed him—and he was one of his companions. Abdullah ibn Ubayy became angry and said: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse from around him'—meaning the Bedouins—and they used to attend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at mealtimes. Abdullah said: 'When they disperse from Muhammad's presence, bring the food to Muhammad, so that he and those with him may eat.' Then he said to his companions: 'If you return to al-Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.'"

Zayd said: "I was riding behind my uncle [in al-Tirmidhi: 'behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)'], and I heard Abdullah ibn Ubayy, so I informed my uncle, who went and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for him, and he swore and denied it." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and declared me a liar." He said: "Then my uncle came to me and said: 'What did you intend? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has come to hate you and has declared you a liar, and the hypocrites [in al-Tirmidhi: 'the Muslims'] too.'" He said: "Such a grief fell upon me from their audacity as had not fallen upon anyone else." He said: "While I was travelling with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, my head was drooping from grief, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me, pulled my ear, and smiled in my face. Nothing could have pleased me more than to have had eternal life in this world." Then Abu Bakr caught up with me and said: "What did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to you?" I said: "He said nothing except that he pulled my ear and smiled in my face." He said: "Rejoice!" Then Umar caught up with me, and I told him the same as I had told Abu Bakr. When we arose in the morning, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Munafiqun. Abu Isa (al-Tirmidhi) said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman was asked about the hypocrite, and he said: "He is the one who professes Islam but does not act upon it. And today they are worse than they were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because they used to conceal it, whereas today they display it."

In the two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." And from Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has four traits is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he gives it up: when he is entrusted he betrays, when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he breaks it, and when he disputes he behaves wickedly." He (peace be upon him) informed that whoever combines these traits is a hypocrite, and his report is true.

It is also narrated from al-Hasan that this hadith was mentioned to him, and he said: "The children of Ya'qub spoke and lied, promised and broke their promise, and were entrusted and betrayed." This statement of the Prophet (ﷺ) was only given as a warning to the Muslims and a caution that they not become accustomed to these traits, out of fear that they might lead them to hypocrisy. The meaning is not that whoever exhibits these traits without choice or habituation is a hypocrite. The matter has already been discussed comprehensively in Surah Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), and praise be to Allah. [See vol. 8, p. 212.]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "The believer, when he speaks, is truthful; when he promises, he fulfils; and when he is entrusted, he is faithful." The meaning is: the complete believer, when he speaks, is truthful. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah."﴾ It has been said: the meaning of "nashhad" is "nahlif" (we swear). So the swearing is expressed by the word testimony, because each of swearing and testimony is an affirmation of a matter that is unseen. From this is the saying of Qays ibn Dhurayh:

"And I call Allah to witness that I love her... so this is hers from me, but what does she have for me?"

It is also possible that this is to be taken at its apparent meaning: that they testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), acknowledging faith and disavowing hypocrisy from themselves, and this is the more likely interpretation.

﴿And Allah knows that you are His Messenger﴾ as they themselves said with their tongues.

﴿And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars﴾, that is, in what they displayed of their testimony and their oaths with their tongues. Al-Farra' said: "And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars" with their inner hearts; so the lying refers to the hearts. This indicates that faith is the assent of the heart, and that true speech is the speech of the heart. Whoever says something while believing its opposite is a liar. This meaning has been discussed comprehensively at the beginning of al-Baqarah. It has also been said: Allah refuted them regarding their oaths, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They swear by Allah that they are surely of you, but they are not of you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 56].

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 2:

There are three issues in this.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, meaning as a cover (sutrah). It does not refer to their saying "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." Rather, it refers to the occasion of the revelation of the verse, as mentioned by al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi, concerning Ibn Ubayy, who swore that he had not said it, when he had said it. Al-Dahhak said: it means their swearing by Allah that they are indeed of you. It was also said: it means their oaths mentioned by the Lord in Surat Bara'a (al-Tawbah), when He said: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it]﴾ [al-Tawbah: 74]. [See vol. 8, pp. 164 and 206.]

The second: Whoever says "I swear by Allah" (uqsimu billah), "I bear witness by Allah" (ashhadu billah), "I resolve by Allah" (a'zimu billah), "I take an oath by Allah" (ahlifu billah), or "I swore by Allah" (aqsamtu billah), "I bore witness by Allah" (ashhadtu billah), "I resolved by Allah" (a'zamtu billah), or "I took an oath by Allah" (ahlaftu billah), and mentions "billah" in all of these, there is no disagreement that it is an oath. Likewise according to Malik and his companions, if he says "uqsimu," "ashhadu," "a'zimu," or "ahlifu" without saying "billah," it is an oath if he intended "billah." If he did not intend "billah," it is not an oath. Al-Kiya related this from al-Shafi'i. Al-Shafi'i said: If he says "ashhadu billah" and intends an oath, it is an oath. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: If he says "ashhadu billah laqad kana kadha" (I bear witness by Allah that such-and-such happened), it is an oath; and if he says "ashhadu laqad kana kadha" without intention, it is an oath, due to this verse, because Allah mentioned from them the testimony, then said: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾. According to al-Shafi'i, it is not an oath even if he intends an oath, because the saying of the Exalted: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ does not refer to His saying: ﴿They say: We bear witness﴾, but refers to what is in "Bara'a" from His saying, exalted: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it]﴾ [al-Tawbah: 74].

The third: His saying, exalted: ﴿So they averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾, meaning they turned away, and it is from al-sudud (turning away). Or they diverted the believers from carrying out Allah's judgment upon them, namely killing, taking captives, and seizing wealth, so it is from al-sadd (hindering). Or they prevented people from jihad by staying behind, so that others would follow their example. It was also said: they hindered the Jews and the polytheists from entering Islam, by saying: "Here we are, disbelievers in him; if Muhammad were truly a prophet, he would know this about us and would have made us an example." Then Allah made clear that their condition is not hidden from Him, but His ruling is that whoever manifests faith, the ruling of faith is applied to him outwardly.

(Indeed, evil is what they used to do.) That is, evil are their deeds, the hidden ones: from their hypocrisy, their false oaths, and their hindering from the way of Allah, as deeds.

This is an announcement from Allah, exalted is He, that the hypocrite is a disbeliever, meaning: they affirmed with the tongue and then disbelieved in the heart. It was also said: the verse was revealed concerning a people who believed and then apostatized. ﴿So their hearts were sealed﴾, meaning they were sealed upon disbelief, ﴿so they do not understand﴾ faith or good.

Zayd ibn Ali recited it as: "Allah sealed upon their hearts" (فطبع الله على قلوبهم).

**Qur'an 63:4: "When you see them, their bodies please you"**

He says, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies impress you﴾, meaning their forms and their appearances.

(And if they speak, you listen to their speech): meaning ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. Ibn ʿAbbas said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy was handsome, large-bodied, healthy, fair-faced, and eloquent of tongue. When he spoke, the Prophet (ﷺ) listened to his words. God described him with completeness of form and excellence of expression. Al-Kalbi said: the intended persons are Ibn Ubayy, Jadd ibn Qays, and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr; they had bodies, appearance, and eloquence.

In Sahih Muslim, regarding His saying ﴿as if they were propped-up timbers﴾, he said: "They were men whose appearance was the most beautiful. [God] compared them to propped-up timbers against a wall, who neither hear nor understand: bodies without spirits, figures without minds." It was also said: He likened them to timbers that have been eaten away, propped up by something else, whose inside is not known.

Qunbul, Abu ʿAmr, and al-Kisa'i read *khushubun* (خُشُبٌ) with the *shin* sukun (خُشْبٌ). This is also the reading of al-Baraa ibn ʿAazib and the preference of Abu ʿUbayd, because its singular is *khashabah* (خَشَبَةٌ), as you say *badanah* (بَدَنَةٌ) and *budn* (بُدْنٌ). There is no pattern *faʿalah* in the language pluralized as *fuʿul*. Because of the heaviness of this, one would say *al-budunu* (البُدُنُ), which is read as (*wal-budun*). Al-Yazidi mentioned that it is a collective of *al-khashbaa'* (الخشباء), like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and gardens dense with trees﴾, whose singular is *ḥadīqah ghalbaa'* (حديقة غلباء).

The rest read it with *shin* emphasized (خُشُبٌ with a doubled consonant pattern, i.e., *khushub* as the plural). This is the transmission of al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir, and of ʿAyyash from Abu ʿAmr, and most transmissions from ʿAasim. Abu Hatim preferred it, as if it were the plural of *khishab* and *khashab*, like *thamarah* (ثمرة), *thimar*, and *thumur*. If you wish, you may take the plural of *khashabah* as *khashabah*, as they said *badanah*, *budn*, and *budun*.

It is also narrated from Ibn al-Musayyib that he read *khashab* with fatha on the *kha'* and *shin*. Sibawayh said: *khashabah* and *khushub*, like *badanah* and *budun*. He said: similarly, without the *ha'*: *asad* and *usud*, *wathan* and *wuthun*. And it is recited *khushub*, which is a plural of a plural: *khashabah*, *khishab*, and *khushub*, like *thamarah*, *thimar*, and *thumur*.

*Al-isnad* (الإسناد) means *al-imalah* (الإمالة), inclination. You say: *asnadtu al-shay'* (أسندت الشيء), meaning I leaned it. *Musannadah* (مسندة) is for intensification, meaning they leaned upon oaths to protect their blood.

**Qur'an 63:4 (continued): "They think every cry is against them"**

He says: ﴿They think every cry is against them; they are the enemy﴾, meaning every cry against them, they are the enemy. The phrase *hum al-ʿaduww* (هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ) is in the position of the second object (*mafʿul thani*), on the basis that the sentence has no pronoun in it. He describes them with cowardice and feebleness. Muqatil and al-Suddi said: when a caller calls out in the camp that an animal has escaped or a lost thing is being sought, they think they are the ones intended, because of the terror in their hearts. As the poet al-Akhtal said:

*You kept thinking every thing after them*
*was horsemen charging at them, and men.*

It was also said: "They think every cry against them is the enemy" is a sentence whose pronoun does not need what follows. Its implied meaning is: they think every cry against them means that they have been noticed and their hypocrisy has been known, because doubt produces fear. Then God resumed addressing His Prophet (ﷺ) and said: ﴿They are the enemy﴾. This is the meaning of the statement of al-Dahhak.

It was also said: they think every cry they hear in the mosque is against them, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) has ordered their killing in it. So they are always fearful that God will send down a command that makes their blood lawful and exposes their secrets. In this sense is the statement of the poet:

*Had it been a sparrow, I would have thought it*
*a marked one calling ʿUbayd and Aznam.*

Aznam is a clan of Banu Yarbuʿ.

Then God described them with His saying: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related it. In His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿so beware of them﴾ there are two interpretations. One: beware of trusting their words or inclining to their speech. Two: beware of what they plot against your enemies and what they discourage among your companions.

**Qur'an 63:4 (continued): "May God destroy them"**

(May God curse them): meaning God curse them, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Abu Malik. It is an expression of blame and reproach. The Arabs say: *qatalahu Allah ma ashaʿarahu* (قاتله الله ما أشعره), "May God curse him, how perceptive he is!", using it in the place of wonder. It was also said: the meaning of *qatalahumu Allah* is: He places them in the position of one whom a dominant enemy fights, because God is dominant over every opponent. This was related by Ibn ʿIsa.

(How are they deluded?): meaning how do they lie, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas. Qatadah said: its meaning is that they turn away from the truth. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that they are turned away from right guidance. It was also said: its meaning is how their minds go astray from this, despite the clarity of the proofs. It is from *al-ifk* (الإفك), which is turning away. And *(anna)* here means *kayfa* (كيف), "how", and this has been mentioned before. [See vol. 3, p. 92 and vol. 4, p. 79.]

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an) on Surah 63, verse 5:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you,"﴾. When the Qur'an was revealed describing them, their clansmen came to them and said: "You have been exposed through hypocrisy (nifaq), so repent to the Messenger of God from hypocrisy and ask him to seek forgiveness for you." So they twisted their heads, meaning they shook them in mockery and refusal. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. It is also related from him that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had a position in every matter that urged obedience to God and His Messenger. It was said to him: "What will that benefit you, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is angry? Go to him so that he may ask forgiveness for you." He refused and said: "I will not go to him."

The occasion of the revelation of these verses was that the Prophet (ﷺ) campaigned against the Banu al-Mustaliq at a water source called "al-Muraysi'," on the side of Qudayd toward the coast. A hired man of 'Umar called Jahjah quarrelled with an ally of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy called Sinan over a water source at "al-Mushallal." Jahjah cried out for the Emigrants (al-Muhajirin), and Sinan cried out for the Helpers (al-Ansar). Jahjah struck Sinan, and 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "Have they really done this? By God, our case and theirs is only as the first one said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.' By God, if we return to Medina, the more honourable (al-a'azz), meaning Ubayy, will surely expel the more humble (al-adhall), meaning Muhammad (ﷺ)." Then he said to his people: "Withhold your provisions from this man, and do not spend on those who are with him, until they disperse and abandon him."

Zayd ibn Arqam, who was of the clan of 'Abd Allah, said: "By God, you are the humble one, despised among your people, while Muhammad (ﷺ) is in honour from the Most Merciful and in the affection of the Muslims. By God, I will never love you after these words of yours." 'Abd Allah said: "Be silent, I was only joking." Zayd informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of his words, and 'Abd Allah swore by God that he had neither done nor said it, so the Prophet (ﷺ) excused him. Zayd said: "I felt grief in my heart and the people blamed me." Then the Surah of the Hypocrites was revealed, confirming Zayd and refuting 'Abd Allah. It was said to 'Abd Allah: "Severe verses have been revealed concerning you, so go to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he may ask forgiveness for you." He twisted his head, and then the verses were revealed. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi related it in substance. It has been mentioned earlier at the beginning of the Surah.

It was also said: "that he may ask forgiveness for you" means "that he may call you to repentance from hypocrisy," because repentance (tawbah) is a form of seeking forgiveness (istighfar).

(And you see them turning away while they are arrogant): that is, they turn away from the Messenger, proud to accept faith.

Nafi' recited "lawaw" (لَوَوْا) with a light pronunciation, while the rest of the readers (al-Baqun) recited it with the intensive form (shaddah). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this and said: "It is a verb for a group." Al-Nahhas said: "He erred in this, because it was revealed about 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy when it was said to him: 'Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you,' and he shook his head in mockery." If it is asked: "How does it report of him with a plural verb?" It is answered: "The Arabs do this when they refer to a person indirectly." Sibawayh cited Hassan's verse:

*You thought that what you did would remain hidden,*
*while among us is a Messenger with whom the revelation is, which exposes it.*

Hassan was addressing Ibn al-Abiraq concerning a theft he had committed in Mecca, and his story is well known.

It is also permissible to report about him and about those who did his action together. It was also said that when Ibn Ubayy twisted his head, he said: "You ordered me to believe, so I have believed; and you ordered me to give the zakat of my wealth, so I have given it. Nothing remains except that I prostrate to Muhammad!"

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾. He means: all of that is the same; your seeking forgiveness benefits them nothing, because Allah will not forgive them. Its parallel is: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah 6], and ﴿It is the same for us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 136]. This has already been discussed earlier [see vol. 13, p. 125].

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, i.e., those whom it has already been decreed in Allah's knowledge that they will die as defiant transgressors.

We mentioned the occasion of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) earlier. Ibn Ubayy said: "Do not spend on those who are with Muhammad until they disperse, until they scatter from him." God, glorified is He, informed them that the treasuries of the heavens and the earth belong to Him, and He spends as He wills.

A man said to Hatim al-Asamm: "From where do you eat?" He said: ﴿And to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth﴾.

Al-Junayd said: "The treasuries of the heavens are the unseen matters, and the treasuries of the earth are the hearts. So He is the Knower of the unseen and the Turner of hearts."

Al-Shibli used to say: ﴿And to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth﴾, so where do you go?

(﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾) that when He intends a matter, He makes it easy.

The speaker is Ibn Ubayy, as mentioned earlier. It was also said that when he said, "The mightier will expel the meaner from it," and returned to Medina, he did not remain for more than a few days before he died. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then asked forgiveness for him and dressed him in his own shirt, and then this verse was revealed: "Allah will never forgive them." All of this has been explained fully in the commentary on Surah Bara'ah (Tawbah) [see vol. 8, p. 218].

It is narrated that Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said to his father: "By He besides whom there is no god, you will not enter Medina until you say that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the mightier and you are the meaner." So he said it. They assumed that might lies in the abundance of wealth and followers, so Allah made clear that might, invincibility and strength belong to Allah.

He warned the believers against the character of the hypocrites, meaning: do not preoccupy yourselves with your wealth as the hypocrites did, when they said, out of stinginess with their wealth: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah" (ﷺ). "...from the remembrance of Allah"—that is, from the Hajj and the zakat. It has also been said: from the recitation of the Qur'an. It has also been said: from constant remembrance (dhikr). It has also been said: from the five daily prayers; this was said by al-Dahhak. Al-Hasan said: all the obligatory duties, as if he said: from obedience to Allah. It has also been said: this is an address to the hypocrites, meaning: you have believed with the tongue, so believe with the heart. "And whoever does that"—that is, whoever preoccupies himself with wealth and children to the neglect of obedience to his Lord—"those are the losers."

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 63, verses 10–11:**

There are four issues (masa'il) in this passage.

**The first issue:** God's words, ﴿And spend of what We have provided you, before death comes to one of you﴾, indicate the obligation to hasten the payment of zakat (obligatory almsgiving), and it is not permissible to delay it at all. The same applies to all acts of worship whose time has been fixed.

**The second issue:** God's words, ﴿and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me to a near term, so I would give charity and be among the righteous"﴾, show that he asks to return to the world in order to do righteous deeds.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Whoever has wealth that is sufficient to bring him to the House of his Lord (the Ka'bah for hajj), or on which zakat is due, and does not do it, will ask to return at the time of death." A man said: "O Ibn Abbas, fear Allah! Only the disbelievers ask to return." He said: "I will recite to you a Qur'an about that: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers. And spend of what We have provided you, before death comes to one of you, and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me to a near term, so I would give charity and be among the righteous,' … up to His words, ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾." He said: "What makes zakat obligatory?" He said: "When the wealth reaches two hundred (dirhams) or more." He said: "What makes hajj obligatory?" He said: "Provision and a mount."

I say: al-Halimi Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan mentioned it in his book (Minhaj al-Din) as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) report. He said: "Ibn Abbas said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever has wealth that is sufficient to bring him to hajj…'" and he mentioned the hadith. Its wording has already been mentioned in Al 'Imran. [[See vol. 4, p. 153.]]

**The third issue:** Ibn al-'Arabi said: "Ibn Abbas took the generality of the verse as applying to obligatory spending only, not to voluntary (nafl) spending. As for his explaining it as zakat, it is entirely correct in general terms, and in quantity by the two hundred (dirhams). As for what he said about hajj, there is a difficulty. If we say that hajj may be performed at a later time (ʿala al-tarakhi), then the case of one who dies in sin before performing hajj is a matter of disagreement among the scholars, so the verse cannot be interpreted in that way. If we say that hajj must be performed immediately (ʿala al-fawr), then the verse in its generality is correct, because whoever is obligated to perform hajj and does not perform it will meet from Allah what will make him wish that he had returned to perform the acts of worship he left. As for specifying the command with provision and a mount, there is a well-known disagreement among the scholars about that. Ibn Abbas's statement has no place in this, because the threat of return and warning does not apply to matters on which scholars exercise independent judgment (mujtahad fihā) or on which they differ, but only to matters on which there is consensus. The correct view is that it covers the obligatory spending, however it is disbursed, either by consensus (ijma') or by the explicit text of the Qur'an, because whatever goes beyond that is not one to which the realization of the threat applies."

**The fourth issue:** God's word, ﴿lawla﴾, means "hallā" (why not / if only), in which case it is interrogative. It has also been said that it is not a connecting particle (la sila), in which case the statement has the sense of wishing (tamanni). ﴿Fa-asaddaqa﴾ is in the accusative as an answer to the wish, introduced by the fa'. ﴿Wa-akun﴾ is coordinated with ﴿fa-asaddaqa﴾, and this is the reading of Abu 'Amr, Ibn Muhaysin and Mujahid. The rest of the readers read ﴿wa-akun﴾ in the jussive, coordinated with the position of the fa' (ʿalā mawḍiʿ al-fāʾ), because if the fa' were not there, the verb ﴿asaddaqa﴾ would be jussive, meaning ﴿asaddaq﴾. A similar case is ﴿whoever Allah leaves astray, there is none to guide him, and He leaves them﴾ (al-A'raf 7:186), according to those who read it in the jussive.

Ibn Abbas said: "This verse is more severe for the people of tawhid (monotheism), because no one who has a good standing with Allah in the Hereafter wishes to return to the world or to be delayed in it." I say: except the martyr (shahid), for he wishes to return so that he may be killed again, because of the honour he sees.

﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, of good and evil. The common reading is with the ta' (second person, "you"). Abu Bakr, on the authority of 'Asim, and al-Sulami read it with the ya' (third person, "He"), referring to the one who died and made this statement.

*The surah is complete, by the praise and help of Allah.*

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 63, verses 10–11:**

There are four issues (masa'il) in this passage.

**The first issue:** God's words, ﴿And spend of what We have provided you, before death comes to one of you﴾, indicate the obligation to hasten the payment of zakat (obligatory almsgiving), and it is not permissible to delay it at all. The same applies to all acts of worship whose time has been fixed.

**The second issue:** God's words, ﴿and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me to a near term, so I would give charity and be among the righteous"﴾, show that he asks to return to the world in order to do righteous deeds.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Whoever has wealth that is sufficient to bring him to the House of his Lord (the Ka'bah for hajj), or on which zakat is due, and does not do it, will ask to return at the time of death." A man said: "O Ibn Abbas, fear Allah! Only the disbelievers ask to return." He said: "I will recite to you a Qur'an about that: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers. And spend of what We have provided you, before death comes to one of you, and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me to a near term, so I would give charity and be among the righteous,' … up to His words, ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾." He said: "What makes zakat obligatory?" He said: "When the wealth reaches two hundred (dirhams) or more." He said: "What makes hajj obligatory?" He said: "Provision and a mount."

I say: al-Halimi Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan mentioned it in his book (Minhaj al-Din) as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) report. He said: "Ibn Abbas said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever has wealth that is sufficient to bring him to hajj…'" and he mentioned the hadith. Its wording has already been mentioned in Al 'Imran. [[See vol. 4, p. 153.]]

**The third issue:** Ibn al-'Arabi said: "Ibn Abbas took the generality of the verse as applying to obligatory spending only, not to voluntary (nafl) spending. If we say that hajj may be performed at a later time (ʿala al-tarakhi), then the case of one who dies in sin before performing hajj is a matter of disagreement among the scholars, so the verse cannot be interpreted in that way. If we say that hajj must be performed immediately (ʿala al-fawr), then the verse in its generality is correct, because whoever is obligated to perform hajj and does not perform it will meet from Allah what will make him wish that he had returned to perform the acts of worship he left.
